harmonicFunction: A (I) - Tonic chord enriched with open 2nd string (Asus2) and 3rd fret (A7) hammer-ons
Em7 (v7) - Minor fifth chord creating a haunting, blues-inflected bittersweet emotion
D (IV) - Subdominant chord providing melodic warmth and redemption
G (bVII) - Borrowed Mixolydian chord in the chorus adding dramatic emotional weight

techniques.name: James Taylor Signature Clawhammer Fingerstyle
techniques.description: Using the flesh of the thumb for bass notes while curling index and middle fingers upward to pluck treble strings, embellished with rapid hammer-ons from open strings to chord tones

sequence: Place capo on 3rd fret and check tuning
Pluck open 5th string bass note with thumb
Hammer on 2nd finger onto 3rd string 2nd fret and 3rd finger onto 2nd string 2nd fret
Slide into open Em7 and resolve through ringing D major
tips: Use the flesh of your fingers rather than long nails for Taylor's trademark woody, round acoustic tone
Keep the tempo relaxed at 76 BPM — never rush the conversational timing
Let open high E and B strings ring as drones throughout transitions

beginner.title: Master Capo 3 Chords
steps: Place capo on 3rd fret and tune carefully
Learn open A, Em7, D, and Bm chord shapes
Strum through the verse progression at 65 BPM
Bring up to album tempo of 76 BPM

intermediate.title: Incorporate James Taylor's Fingerstyle
steps: Practice the signature hammer-on into open A
Work on the chorus transition D → Bm → A → Em7

advanced.title: Authentic Acoustic Interpretation
steps: Nail James Taylor's subtle conversational timing and rubato
Perform complete vocal and acoustic accompaniment
Deliver an intimate, deeply moving performance

commonMistakes: Playing with rigid fingerpicks — Taylor's tone requires bare finger flesh
Rushing the 76 BPM tempo — ballad spacing gives the lyrics room to breathe
Barring the A chord flatly instead of using open string hammer-ons
practiceRoutine: 2 minutes: Capo 3 tuning and finger warm-up
5 minutes: Signature A chord hammer-on drill
5 minutes: Verse fingerpicking cycle at 76 BPM
5 minutes: Chorus chord transitions (D → Bm → A)
focusAreas: Bare finger flesh attack for warm woody tone
metronomeWork: Practice at 65 BPM with metronome clicks on all beats
Advance to 76 BPM once thumb independence is solid
Practice with clicks on beats 2 and 4 to develop relaxed folk sway
